bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42516694 (haproxy): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_cfg_parser [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42516694
bug_description.normalized: The saved PoC is an 18-line HAProxy configuration file. After `readcfgfile()` trims line 1's leading spaces, `*line == '['` sends that line to `cfg_parse_scope()` instead of `parse_line()`, matching the first sanitizer alert about an invalid scope-name character. The first `parse_line()` sizing pass therefore happens on later line 2, a lone backslash, with `outline == NULL`; `parse_line()` reports `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE` and `outlen == 2`, so `readcfgfile()` rounds that requirement up to a reusable 1024-byte `outline`. When the loop later reaches the 1971-byte line 17, it calls `parse_line()` again with that non-NULL 1024-byte buffer. `EMIT_CHAR` sets `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE` once `outpos` reaches 1024 but keeps advancing `outpos`; a later ordinary whitespace separator stores `args[arg] = out + outpos`, and the final `if (arg < argsmax && out && *(args[arg]))` dereferences that pointer at `outline + 1428`, which is 404 bytes past the allocation ASan reports. The fix removes the dereference and compares pointers instead (`args[arg] != out + outpos - 1`).

fine_trace.code: while (fgets(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, f) != NULL) {
fine_trace.note: Source. `fgets()` copies attacker-controlled configuration bytes from the fuzzed file into `thisline`. In the saved witness, line 1 begins with spaces then `[`, line 2 is a lone `\`, and line 17 is 1971 bytes long.

On witness line 1, trimming leading spaces makes `line` point at `[`, so `readcfgfile()` routes that line to `cfg_parse_scope()` instead of `parse_line()`. This matches the first sanitizer alert about `' '` not being permitted in the scope name and leaves line 2 as the first line that can size `outline`.

On witness line 2 (`\`), `outline == NULL` and `outlinesize == 0`, so `readcfgfile()` invokes `parse_line()` as a sizing pass with no output buffer. Because `PARSE_OPT_BKSLASH` is enabled, the lone backslash is emitted literally and then the terminating NUL is emitted, so `parse_line()` returns `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE` and `outlen == 2` while the final `out && *(args[arg])` test short-circuits on `out == NULL`.

The sizing pass on line 2 reports `outlen == 2`, so this branch rounds that requirement up to 1024 bytes and allocates `outline = my_realloc2(NULL, 1024)`. Because `outline` is declared outside the line loop, the same 1024-byte buffer is reused on later lines.

When the loop later reaches witness line 17, `line` aliases the attacker-controlled 1971-byte string while `outline` is non-NULL and `outlen = outlinesize = 1024`. `readcfgfile()` therefore calls `parse_line()` on the long line with the reused 1024-byte buffer that was allocated from line 2.

Inside `parse_line()`, `outmax` is the caller's 1024-byte `outlen`. Once emitted output reaches offset 1024, `EMIT_CHAR` sets `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE` and stops writing into `outline`, but it still increments `outpos` while parsing the rest of line 17.

After step 6 has let `outpos` run past `outmax`, a later ordinary whitespace separator on line 17 starts a new argument. The witness line contains hundreds of literal spaces and no `}` bytes for `${...[*]}` word expansion, so this plain-space splitter records `args[arg] = out + outpos`; ASan's crash address shows the stored pointer was `outline + 1428`, i.e. 404 bytes past the 1024-byte allocation.

Root cause. The final non-empty-argument test only checks that `arg < argsmax` and `out` is non-NULL before dereferencing `args[arg]` to see whether the last argument is empty. When step 7 has already advanced `args[arg]` beyond `outline`, this dereference turns the emptiness check into an out-of-bounds read instead of the pointer comparison used by the fix (`args[arg] != out + outpos - 1`).

Sink. Evaluating this expression reads one byte from `outline + 1428`, which is 404 bytes to the right of the 1024-byte region allocated at `readcfgfile:1870`; AddressSanitizer reports that exact heap-buffer-overflow READ at `src/tools.c:5758`.

allocation_context.note: `outline = my_realloc2(outline, outlinesize);` is the 1024-byte heap allocation whose extent ASan reports.

format.name: HAProxy config file
format.contract: Use the saved 18-line witness. Line 1 must still begin with spaces and then `[` so `readcfgfile()` trims it and routes it to `cfg_parse_scope()`. Line 2 must still be a single backslash so it is the first non-empty line that reaches `parse_line()` with `outline == NULL`, yielding `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE`, `outlen == 2`, and a rounded 1024-byte `outline`. The later 1971-byte line 17 must then be parsed with that reused buffer so `outpos` advances beyond 1024, `args[arg]` is recorded at the ASan-reported offset `outline + 1428`, and the final `*(args[arg])` emptiness check in `parse_line()` executes.
